transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-15
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Arielle Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (NewFound Head of ML), Oliver Grant (Platform Eng), Sofia Reyes (Security)

Summary: discovery focused on Dedicated/reserved GPUs for inference; isolation needs for PHI workloads, burst capacity expectations and fallback to hosted; security/compliance (SOC2, KMS) discussed. Action items noted.

Topics: dedicated reservation sizing, tenant isolation, burst capacity model, VPC/on-prem options, encryption/KMS and audit logs, pilot/benchmark plan, timeline and cost concerns.

Transcript:
[00:00] Arielle Park: all right folks thanks for taking the time. um i'm Arielle, i'm the account lead on this. we have Marcus from our infra team as well. how's everyone doing?
[00:18] Priya Shah: good, thanks. excited to dig in. we run medical summarization and triage so there's PHI in scope, which i know complicates things.
[00:28] Marcus Li: yeah good to meet you Priya. i mostly focus on inference ops, routing and the dedicated runtime — curious to hear your qps and latency targets.
[00:38] Oliver Grant: hi, Oliver here. platform team. for starters we expect around 150 qps at peak across bursts for a week, steady state maybe 20 qps, 99th latency target ideally sub 300ms for short prompts, longer for batch.
[00:52] Arielle Park: okay that's helpful — 150 qps peak with bursts. are bursts predictable scheduled batches or traffic spikes?
[01:05] Priya Shah: a mix. some scheduled nightly bulk de-id jobs, and occasional spikes when we open a new clinic and the traffic replays. bursts could be 5-8x steady state for short windows.
[01:18] Marcus Li: got it. and the data sensitivity — PHI — are you constrained to VPC/on-prem, or can you consider dedicated in our hosted with private network peering?
[01:31] Sofia Reyes: security: our compliance team is pushing for customer-managed keys and network isolation; ideally private deployment in our cloud account or an on-prem box. SOC2 is table stakes.
[01:44] Arielle Park: understood. Redwood Private has options: private control plane with customer-managed KMS and VPC peering; Dedicated Reserved is a managed pool per tenant that can also use VPC peering. we'll show specifics after.
[01:56] Oliver Grant: when you say "reserved" is that physical GPU isolation per tenant or logical isolation with multi-tenant drivers?
[02:07] Marcus Li: good question. we offer both patterns depending on contract and SKUs. reserved pools can be single-tenant nodes (dedicated GPUs) or shared nodes with strong tenant isolation using cgroups and nvlink isolation. for PHI we'd typically recommend single-tenant nodes.
[02:25] Priya Shah: single-tenant nodes seems safer. how does bursting work then? do we get burst credits or additional preemptible capacity?
[02:36] Arielle Park: we do burst capacity in two ways: scheduled buffer you reserve as burstable capacity in the contract, and on-demand cross-tenant burst to a lower-cost compatible variant if single-tenant is exhausted. fallback can be to a quantized model variant or a hosted fallback in another region — depends on your policy.
[02:55] Oliver Grant: fallback to hosted — wouldn't that leak PHI?
[02:59] Marcus Li: there are ways to avoid that. for PHI we can do region-locked hosted fallback inside your VPC or have a private-hosted instance tied to your org and same KMS. otherwise we fallback to a compatible model in your private deployment.
[03:16] Sofia Reyes: we need KMS/HSM integration and full audit logs. retention policies must be configurable. we also need SSO/SAML and RBAC controls.
[03:29] Arielle Park: entirely doable. we integrate with common KMS providers and can enable HSM for key wrapping. audit logs are exported to your cloud logging; retention is configurable with add-on. SSO/SAML and fine-grained RBAC are standard for enterprise plans.
[03:44] Priya Shah: cost is a concern. dedicated GPUs are expensive — what's the unit economics vs hosted?
[03:52] Marcus Li: ballpark: dedicated reserved capacity reduces unit GPU cost at scale because you amortize across committed hours; hosted is higher per-token but zero ops overhead. with 150 qps bursts you may still need a mix: reserved for baseline plus burst buffer. quantization (4-bit) and batching also help.
[04:08] Oliver Grant: what's Redwood's typical batch sizes and latency tradeoffs? we care about 99th pctl.
[04:16] Marcus Li: typical continuous batching is dynamic; for sub-300ms 99th we aim to keep batch sizes small for low-latency traffic. for the nightly bulk jobs we'll open larger batch windows. we can tune the scheduler per route.
[04:30] Priya Shah: you mentioned quantized variants — does that degrade accuracy for our clinical summarization? we need to keep F1 within 1-2% of baseline.
[04:40] Marcus Li: there's a trade, yes. our Optimize toolkit recommends quantization per workload and can run A/B evals. for clinical NER/summarization we often keep full-fp or 8-bit while using batching and KV cache to reduce cost. we'll include model-quality notes in the benchmark.
[04:55] Arielle Park: can you sketch the stakeholders and timeline? are you looking to pilot in the next quarter?
[05:03] Priya Shah: timeline: pilot within 4-6 weeks if cost and security checks out. stakeholders: me, Oliver for infra, Sofia for security, then legal for DPA.
[05:12] Oliver Grant: for pilot we'd want a fenced environment with sample PHI-scrubbed data, and a runbook for failover.
[05:20] Marcus Li: we'll propose a benchmark plan: synthetic traffic matching your qps profile + a batch job. recommend a short canary with dedicated single-tenant nodes then load ramp.
[05:30] Arielle Park: good. quick question about model pinning and rollouts: do you need version pinning or automatic rollbacks?
[05:38] Priya Shah: yes PINNING is required for clinical models. we need controlled rollouts, canary and rollback hooks, and deterministic audit trails for which model served which request.
[05:48] Marcus Li: we support per-route model pinning and rollout policies with tracing. each response includes model version metadata that we persist to your logs.
[05:57] Oliver Grant: what about peak capacity planning — if we reserve too few GPUs we'll suffer latency at peak; if too many we're overpaying. do you have a sizing playbook?
[06:08] Arielle Park: we do. it'll be part of what we send: a reservation sizing worksheet that maps qps/latency targets to GPU counts across different model families and sequence lengths. we also include a recommended burst buffer percentage.
[06:21] Priya Shah: can we run a dry-run with a representative model? maybe a smaller distil-type first then a full model test.
[06:30] Marcus Li: absolutely. we usually run a 2-phase benchmark: phase 1 correctness and latency with a distilled variant, phase 2 capacity and failover with the target model. that helps bound costs.
[06:42] Sofia Reyes: about network isolation: we need end-to-end encryption and no internet egress unless explicitly allowed. can we control egress rules?
[06:52] Marcus Li: yes, VPC peering plus private link options. egress can be disabled and logs stored in your logging project.
[07:01] Priya Shah: legal and procurement will ask about indemnity and data residency. do you support EU-only regions if needed?
[07:09] Arielle Park: yes, we have regions in NA and EU and can pin workloads. Redundancy across regions is optional and based on your SLA choice.
[07:17] Oliver Grant: do you do warm KV cache preloading for cold-start heavy models? we noticed big latency spikes on cold starts in our tests.
[07:26] Marcus Li: yes, we support KV cache preloading and gradual warmers; for dedicated nodes we can persist cold cache snapshots to reduce warm start spikes.
[07:36] Priya Shah: what telemetry do you expose? token-level cost, per-route P95/P99, tracing?
[07:44] Arielle Park: full telemetry in Redwood Console: token breakdown, per-route latency percentiles, traces and sample request logs. console can be integrated to your SIEM.
[07:53] Oliver Grant: audits — do you provide immutable audit logs for admin actions?
[07:58] Marcus Li: yes admin actions are logged with user context and can be exported. we also support approver workflows for production configuration changes.
[08:08] Sofia Reyes: ok good. now two operational questions: how do you handle driver updates and CUDA/kernel patches on dedicated single-tenant nodes? we need maintenance windows.
[08:20] Marcus Li: maintenance windows are configurable per tenant. for single-tenant nodes you can choose a maintenance cadence; we offer deadlines for critical patches and can do in-place rolling updates or freeze windows for clinical ops.
[08:33] Priya Shah: if we have a blackout period for production (e.g., during a conference release month) can we lock changes?
[08:40] Arielle Park: yes you can freeze configuration and pin versions. we also offer a mitigation policy for emergency rollbacks.
[08:48] Oliver Grant: what about runbook for cross-availability failover? e.g., if a whole rack has power issues, how do we move traffic?
[08:58] Marcus Li: we recommend multi-AZ deployments and autoswarm policies that spin up nodes in another AZ or region; failover can be automated or manual based on your SLOs. for single-tenant nodes we'd provision standby nodes in a secondary AZ if you opt-in.
[09:13] Priya Shah: can you give a rough monthly cost estimate for baseline plus burst capacity for 150 peak qps? we need ballpark numbers for procurement.
[09:22] Arielle Park: I can rough it now but we'll send a worksheet. ballpark: dedicated baseline to meet steady state might be X GPUs (we'll calculate) costing approx $Yk/month; burst buffer as reserved credit or preemptible slots varies. i'll follow up with detailed numbers.
[09:34] Oliver Grant: please include comparison of fully private VPC vs dedicated in your hosted environment in that worksheet.
[09:40] Arielle Park: will do.
[09:43] Marcus Li: quick technical note: for high qps short requests we recommend models with shorter context windows unless you need full transcripts; that reduces memory and improves packing.
[09:55] Priya Shah: for our summarization we often need 2k context. how does that change GPU choices?
[10:02] Marcus Li: larger context increases memory and reduces the effective tokens/sec per GPU. we'll include that in the sizing — likely larger-memory SKUs or multi-GPU partitioning.
[10:12] Oliver Grant: any SLA for 99th percentile latency?
[10:17] Arielle Park: SLA depends on plan. Dedicated enterprise plans can include custom latency SLOs and financial-backed SLAs. we'll map that in the proposal.
[10:24] Sofia Reyes: compliance: can we get a copy of your SOC2 report and pen test summary?
[10:29] Arielle Park: yes — will share SOC2 and summarized pen-test results in the security packet.
[10:34] Priya Shah: we want to avoid any data exfiltration risk during benchmark. can you run benchmarks in our VPC with scrubbed data?
[10:42] Marcus Li: we can — or we can run with synthetic data that mimics distributions. both are options, and we can do the runs inside your account.
[10:50] Oliver Grant: on the billing model — is it monthly committed or hourly reserved?
[10:55] Arielle Park: typically monthly/annual commits for discounted reserved capacity; we also support monthly flex with overage at higher rate. for pilot we can do short-term reservations.
[11:05] Priya Shah: legal will want a DPA + clear data residency clauses.
[11:10] Arielle Park: noted. we'll include a DPA template and data residency options.
[11:15] Oliver Grant: one more: how do you measure model drift and quality regressions after rollouts? we need automatic alerts.
[11:22] Marcus Li: Redwood Optimize supports quality monitoring: eval suites, prompt-anchored baselines, regression alerts and rollback automation. we'll instrument that in pilot.
[11:32] Priya Shah: great. what's the recommended minimum commitment to get single-tenant isolation?
[11:38] Arielle Park: depends on GPU SKU; often a 6-12 month reserved contract or a higher monthly commit for enterprise. for pilot we can do a short-term dedicated carve-out.
[11:50] Oliver Grant: Can we schedule the benchmark run next Thursday morning?
[11:54] Marcus Li: i have a slot — we can tentatively book Thu 09:00 UTC. Oliver, can you confirm?
[12:01] Oliver Grant: yes i'll confirm by EOD tomorrow.
[12:05] Arielle Park: awesome. quick recap and next steps: we'll send the reservation sizing worksheet, SOC2/security packet, and proposed benchmark plan + datasets. Marcus will lead the benchmark. Oliver will confirm QPS details and pilot window. Priya will loop legal.
[12:20] Priya Shah: thanks everyone.
[12:22] Sofia Reyes: thanks.
[12:25] Arielle Park: thanks all — we'll follow up with the materials.

End of transcript.
